articles.title: What time is Cubs' game with Orioles? Forecasted rain moves series finale to afternoon in Baltimore
articles.description:
BALTIMORE – The Cubs and Orioles will play a matinee with rain in the forecast Thursday night in Maryland.

An ugly outlook for baseball forced a change from a night game to an afternoon start, with first pitch moving from 5:35 p.m. Central to 12:35 p.m. Central.

The two teams sat through a nearly hourlong delay before the start of the first game of this three-game series Tuesday night.

The Cubs will go for a three-game sweep of the Orioles on Thursday after taking the first two games in the series.

articles.title: The great carbon capture con: behold the wasted billions Burnham could claw back | George Monbiot
articles.description: There are far better ways to tackle climate breakdown, but successive governments have chosen to listen to the fossil fuel companies instead The new prime minister will be looking for money? Well, here’s £21.7bn lying on the ground. The government could cancel its deranged, disastrous carbon capture and storage (CCS) programme at no cost to public welfare: in fact, it would greatly reduce the harm we will suffer. Sorry, did I say £21.7bn? That’s the figure the government has been putting in its press releases for spending on this programme between now and 2050. But this covers only the first phase of the project. The climate experts Dr Andrew Boswell and Simon Oldridge worked through the data produced by the government’s Climate Change Committee, which was scattered across different spreadsheets, and discovered that the projected cost of the full CCS programme between now and 2050 is £264bn . George Monbiot is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

articles.title: Horoscope for Wednesday, July 08, 2026
articles.description:
Moon Alert

Avoid shopping (except food and gas) and important decisions from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. After that, the moon moves from Aries into Taurus.

Aries (March 21-April 19)

An average day

Keep your digs tidy and your fridge stocked because relatives and people from your past might be camped on your doorstep. This could be due to family reunions, visitors or guests. This is a good time to tackle home repairs that have needed your attention.

Taurus (April 20-May 20)

A positive day

Allow extra time when you're traveling this week because Mercury retrograde will create breakdowns with cars and trucks, as well as missed buses and all kinds of delays to your transportation plans. Likewise, communications with others will be like two ships passing in the night. Be extra clear when talking to everyone.

Gemini (May 21-June 20)

An average day

Checks might be late in the mail, and other delays to financial matters are likely, along with mistakes with your credit cards, your bank accounts or anything to do with your cash flow and finances. Double-check all your financial dealings. (You snooze — you lose.)

Cancer (June 21-July 22)

A positive day

Mercury is retrograde in your sign until July 23, giving you the advantage of being able to finish old business that's already on your plate. However, you face the disadvantage of suffering from goofy mistakes, delays, mixed-up communications and misplaced items.

Leo (July 23-Aug. 22)

An average day

Mercury retrograde might bring opportunities to explore spiritual issues from the past. It might reveal secrets about yourself and others. Admittedly, it might make you feel that you're not in control of your world. (Is anyone?)

Virgo (Aug. 23-Sept. 22)

A positive day

Old friends and acquaintances from the past are back in your world now. Some contacts that you will hear from might be through clubs, groups and organizations. The reconnection might be online, in person or in your dreams. (It's good to have history with people.)

Libra (Sept. 23-Oct. 22)

An average day

Very likely, you're thinking about or running into parents, ex-bosses and authority figures from your past — in person, online or in your dreams. You might even have an imaginary conversation with someone. (Those are fun because now you can think of the right thing to say.)

Scorpio (Oct. 23-Nov. 21)

An average day

Travel delays will likely occur for some travelers. Double-check itineraries and small details if you are going somewhere. It's best if you travel to a place you've been before because then you are "returning." This is a great time to study history and issues from the past.

Sagittarius (Nov. 22-Dec. 21)

An average day

Double-check all transactions and financial negotiations with others because Mercury retrograde will encourage errors and hiccups. Do not assume everything is correct. On the upside, Mercury retrograde will help you finish matters related to inheritances and shared property.

Capricorn (Dec. 22-Jan. 19)

A positive day

Mercury retrograde will attract news about ex-partners and old friends. In some cases, you will encounter these people in person or online. You might hear about what they're up to, or they might come to you in your dreams and thoughts.

Aquarius (Jan. 20-Feb. 18)

An average day

This particular Mercury retrograde will be challenging for you because it will affect your job, your work and even your health. Expect silly errors, misplaced paperwork, delays and equipment breakdowns. However, the good news is Mercury retrograde can help you finish old projects.

Pisces (Feb. 19-March 20)

A positive day

Old flames are back in your world, either in your thoughts, your dreams, online or in person. Be smart and look your best when you go out because you'll feel better if you run into someone important from your past. (We all like to look good.)

If today is your birthday

Actor Kevin Bacon (1958), shares your birthday today. You are strong-willed, dynamic and purposeful. You have artistic and practical skills. This is a year of learning and teaching. Take time to renew your spiritual or religious beliefs. Explore philosophies that give you better self-awareness and get you closer to the true meaning of your life.

articles.title: Birdwatch: A yellowhammer cheer squad on my cycle around Suffolk
articles.description: That characteristic song was an unexpected delight alongside the chiffchaffs, blackcaps and whitethroats too With hindsight, the late June heatwave was not the ideal time for my (very) old schoolmates and me to be cycling around Suffolk. Yet, despite the searing heat and the lateness of the season, the woods and hedgerows were still awash with birdsong. Chirping chiffchaffs, melodic blackcaps and warbling whitethroats were everywhere, while swallows twittered over fields and swifts screamed past rooftops in the towns and villages we rode through. I even saw a cuckoo – which I momentarily mistook for a sparrowhawk – flying fast and low across the road. Continue reading...
